profile.headline: Model-Based Dev Ops SW Engineer
profile.summary:
I empower aerospace engineers to do more of what they love: make planes fly.


I started small. As a side hustle, I automated tedious tasks in my team’s day-to-day work like parsing requirement markups and routing Simulink signals. My contributions were quickly recognized; my manager even went so far as to say “If I could hire 3 more engineers just like you, I would.” Encouraged by the positive feedback and joy of applying my coding skills, I took it to the next level. I spent my after-work hours earning a certificate in Python, which exposed me to a plethora of new concepts and skills from test-driven development and object-oriented programming to SQL and django. 


From there, I broadened my impact by joining my current team, MBD Ops, which is laying the foundation for the future of flight control software development for the entirety of Boeing Commercial Airplanes. From building gitlab pipelines and docker containers, to writing flight software for customer projects, I’m continuing to drive improvements within my team and the greater company. I also remain dedicated to expanding my software engineering knowledge outside of work. I’m currently wrapping up a 3 course certificate in Software Development and Design Essentials which has built up my foundations in critical areas such as algorithms, data structures, and big O analyses. 


I’m excited to continue growing and applying my skills to help others. Please reach out to me on LinkedIn for any new opportunities.

positions.title: Software Engineer - MBD Ops
positions.description: As a member of the 4-person agile development team, MBD Ops, I have the opportunity to pave the way for Boeing to develop model-based flight control software in house. My team and I are working hard to establish the enterprise standards and tooling that make Boeing Commercial Airplane's goal of vertical software development a reality.

positions.title: Flight Controls Engineer - 777X Folding Wingtip
positions.description:
As a member of the 3-person FWT Problem Report (PR) sub-team, I 
- Analyzed root causes, tested, and reviewed solutions to 10+ FWT Problem 
Reports (PR’s) utilizing MATLAB, Simulink and airplane-level simulations
- Decomposed system requirements to verify PR solutions met intent 
- Interfaced with customers to understand their needs and generate software requirements 
- Supported certification of FWT software by refactoring Simulink Stateflow models to close 
structural coverage gaps while maintaining existing functionality 
- Authored and adapted 20+ requirement based scenario file scripts which performed integrated system-level testing of software designs 
- Mentored and guided newer engineers in learning FWT software and authoring system tests 
- Developed custom Python and MATLAB tools to improve everyday workflow efficiency (60 - 80% time savings on individual tasks) 
- Retrofitted existing model coverage tooling to make a flexible system that all teams could use

positions.title: Test Engineer Intern
positions.description:
As part of a team of 5 Test Engineers, I supported projects for a variety of PacSci customers in the aerospace and defense industry. Some of my accomplishments include the following:  
-	Designed a vibration fixture to secure 8 mild detonating cord lines for test 
-	Self-taught Keysight VEE Pro 
-	Utilized VEE to edit and improve the automation of test data collection and analysis 
-	Updated test procedures to meet current military standards 
-	Created skyline vibration profiles to be used in lot acceptance tests 
-	Participated in test readiness reviews prior to lot acceptance tests 
-	Authored test requests and test reports for a variety of products 
-	Shadowed test technicians to learn how test set-ups could best be improved

positions.title: Mechanical Project Engineer Co-op
positions.description:
As a co-op, I participated in and led a variety of projects including the following: 
-	Led the design of a $250,000 2-axis adhesive application robot 
-	Designed and commissioned a motor and gear box skid that allowed line speed to be increased by 50 ft/s, yielding 15% more product for every minute of full speed run time 
-	Researched, ordered, tested, and commissioned 2 pressure transducers, a flow meter, and a control valve to improve GAF’s water reclaim system 
-	Improved communication skills by collaborating with team members from a variety of engineering and non-engineering backgrounds 
-	Shadowed controls, electrical, project, and maintenance engineers to learn about different engineering perspectives and opportunities

positions.title: Food Delivery Driver
positions.locationName: San Luis Obispo County, California, United States
positions.description:
I worked as a food delivery driver in my spare time while attending CalPoly as a Mechanical Engineering student. In this role, I 
- Built my communication skills by constantly interacting with customers and merchants 
- Learned to manage tasks in parallel by often coordinating several simultaneous orders 
- Improved my time management by completing orders in a timely manner

positions.title: Carpenter's Apprentice
positions.description:
As a carpenter's apprentice during summers and holiday breaks, I acquired hands-on experience working as part of a team to 
- renovate houses 
- remodel kitchens and bathrooms
- build sheds 
- construct outdoor living spaces
